content:
clare.marketing: Quick heads-up — saw a spike of ~180 unassigned inbound leads in the last 15m, mostly APAC. Many stuck pending enrichment >120s. Anyone else seeing this?
alex.sales: Yep, seeing same. HubSpot shows owner = unassigned but claim attempts are happening. My guess: rotation jitter causing lock contention.
tori.ops: Good catch. Can you paste a sample lead id so I can grep logs?
clare.marketing: id 6347f2b9. Chart: https://pm.redwood.ai/leadflow/6347f2 (small uptick at 10:12 UTC).
jess-hubspot: Webhook retries from HS look normal. Enrichment lambda is timing out occasionally which delays handoff. Current enrichment TTL = 45s.
sam.revenueops: Short-term mitigation: reduce claim_jitter_ms -> 50ms and set fallback to overflow pool after 20s so leads don't stall. Long-term: apply backpressure on enrichment or cache results.
tori.ops: I can roll a config patch now. Proposed routing config snippet:
```json
{"claim_jitter_ms":50,"claim_timeout_s":20,"overflow_pool":"sdr-overflow"}
```
eng-sre-bot: deploy triggered: routing-config v2026.03.08-8 -> staging (canary enabled) :gear:
alex.sales: I'll watch HubSpot and SFDC. Can we add an auto-assign rule for owner=unassigned >60s as a safety net?
sam.revenueops: Yep, I'll open a ticket to add SF sync rule and update the playbook.
clare.marketing: After the canary (10% -> 50%), assigned rate jumped from 62% -> 94% within 5m. Looks promising.
tori.ops: Rollback plan in place: revert claim_jitter_ms to 500ms if assigned rate drops; script: `ci/rollback routing-config`
eng-sre-bot: canary rollout progress: 10% -> 50% (current), next step in 5m.
jess-hubspot: Note for follow-up: enrichment TTL was bumped to 90s in dev for testing — we should standardize to lower TTL + cache to reduce latency.
sam.revenueops: I'll update the inbound handoff playbook with the new config, add a heartbeat probe for unassigned count, and record SLA for enrichment <30s.
clare.marketing: thanks team. tagging @here so sales/ops see this. :thumbsup:
